Built from evidence/themather/*.md by /resume-evidence:to-brag, after Julia Evans's brag-document template. Do not edit by hand, except inside the user: blocks: change the evidence and rebuild. Draft: 22 of 22 evidence files are not yet verified, so every line below is a draft claim. The files use the older evidence format, with no strength stars, no Impact table and no Learned: lines: bullets keep each file's own order.

At a glance

I worked on 22 client and internal projects between 2023 and 2026, at a Thai software consultancy. I started on Django backends and data analytics, then moved to computer vision, data pipelines and, in 2026, LLM applications and AI infrastructure. My strongest work is a retail-shelf analytics platform I designed and built alone, which a client trialled in 2026-09. I also measured a vision decision model at 89% top-1 accuracy on 739 labelled shelf crops. On a support chatbot, I measured a new retrieval source against the old one and kept it switched off when it scored 56.8% recall@1 against 91.3%.

Projects by theme

Computer vision and video analytics (2023 → 2026)

The work grew from a face-analytics demo for a marketing event (2023) to face-embedding visitor counts from 13 cameras at a motor-show booth (2024), then road-safety and CCTV detection services (2025). In 2026 it became a shelf-analytics platform in client trial, a classroom attention pipeline run on real recordings, and an evaluation of hosted vision decision models.

Retail shelf analytics platform · 2026-03 ~ 2026-11 · shipped, client trial · retail-shelf
My part: sole committer, from design to deployment. The frontend started from an open-source admin template, and the training labels came from a public dataset.

  • Designed and built a multi-tenant shelf-photo analytics platform end to end: one-pass YOLO product/logo/empty detection and DINOv2 brand matching on Modal serverless GPUs, Django REST API, and Next.js dashboards. (B1)
  • Diagnosed a detection accuracy plateau by training YOLO11m-AMF and RF-DETR-small: both reached the same per-class profile (logo AP50 0.54 against product 0.92), tracing the limit to the data. (B5)
  • Built a benchmark system that imports labelled YOLO datasets, runs the production pipeline over them, and scores detection and brand recognition separately, with confusion matrices. (B4)
  • Integrated a hosted vision decision model as a second brand recognizer beside logo matching, with additive storage, a read-time brand-source switch for charts and exports, and fingerprinted re-runs that skip unchanged crops. (B6: unmerged branch, write "integrated" or "prototyped")

Decision-model R&D · 2026-09 ~ 2026-11 · wip · decision-model

  • Evaluated a vision decision model for retail-shelf brand recognition on 739 labelled product crops in 6 categories, reaching 89% top-1 accuracy, with per-brand precision, recall, F1 and confusion matrices. (B1, N1)
  • Compared two vision decision models on the same labelled images: both matched all 44 images against a 200-brand choice set, and the second cost about one-ninth as much per image. (B2)
  • Built an image send policy for a vision model API (resize, JPEG-quality steps, budget halving on 413 retries) and fingerprinted prediction stores, so evaluations re-ran only changed images. (B3)

Classroom video attention analysis · 2026-02 ~ 2026-06 · shipped · classroom
My part: main developer of both repos. A teammate wrote the recorder's Windows build script and some of its styling.

  • Built a RabbitMQ worker pipeline that scored student attention in ~930 webcam recordings (~64 h) from 2 schools, using MediaPipe face landmarks for gaze, blinks, head pose and emotion. (B1)
  • Built a PyQt6 desktop recorder that plays lesson videos while recording the student's webcam, logs playback events to JSON, and switches between Qt and VLC playback backends. (B4)

CCTV people and security analytics · 2025-11 ~ 2026-03 · shipped · cctv
My part: main developer of the backend and the AI service. Teammates built the QR scanner bridge, gate control, the later third-party integration and the frontends.

  • Built face-recognition check-in: InsightFace embeddings of registered visitors stored in pgvector and matched by cosine distance against Hikvision camera webhooks, limited to the appointment day. (B2)
  • Built a multi-camera RTSP detection service with YOLO and ByteTrack that reports weapon, violence and fall events only after an object stays tracked across consecutive frames, attaching face embeddings for later search. (B3)

Road-safety video analytics · 2025-05 ~ 2026-01 · wip, demo stage · road-safety
My part: main developer across most of the system. The backend's first commit came from a company starter template.

  • Designed and built a demo-stage road-safety video analytics system on footage from 3 roadside camera sites: queued detection workers, TimescaleDB time-series storage and a Django REST dashboard API. (B1)
  • Trained an RF-DETR accident-detection model to replace a YOLO model with frequent false positives, and built a lane-straddling detector from per-lane polygon zones and per-track dwell timers. (B3)
  • Wrote an internal Python detection library (composable processing chains, YOLO/RF-DETR behind one interface, ByteTrack tracking, plate OCR), versioned by git tag, ending copy-paste between PoC and production code. (B4)
  • Built LINE and Discord accident alerts with duplicate suppression, replacing pgvector embedding-similarity checks with tracker-ID, site and time-window deduplication. (B5)

Exhibition booth visitor analytics · 2024-11 ~ 2025-02 · shipped · event-booth

  • Designed a unique-visitor estimate from face embeddings: Facenet512 vectors via DeepFace, daily HDBSCAN clustering on cosine distance, and rules that drop staff, screen images, noise and oversized clusters. (B2)
  • Built repeat-visitor search over ChromaDB: each face cluster's average embedding queries similar clusters from other days, giving a per-visitor visit frequency and dwell time. (B3)

Crowd and face-analytics camera PoC · 2023-04 ~ 2024-07 · wip, event demos · crowd-poc
My part: main developer and nearly sole author of the five repos. A teammate wrote the age, gender and emotion model wrappers.

  • Built a real-time audience-analytics demo for a marketing event: Kafka topics carried face results, a pandas analyser aggregated age, gender and emotion, and Flask-SocketIO pushed them to a Next.js dashboard. (B1)
  • Prototyped camera-frame streaming through Kafka to a face-analysis worker running MediaPipe detection and ONNX age, gender and emotion models, switching frames from PNG to JPEG for about 10x smaller messages. (B2, N1)
  • Prototyped short-term visitor re-identification with face embeddings in Weaviate and per-face attribute counts in PyFlink tumbling windows, giving one age, gender and emotion label per visitor on the dashboard. (B3)

LLM applications and AI infrastructure (2026)

In 2026 the work moved to LLM systems: a support chatbot's retrieval and evaluation, a comparison of three RAG strategies, a serving-engine evaluation, decision-model prototypes and a reusable chatbot core. Most of it is research or prototype work, and the bullets say so.

Human-in-the-loop support chatbot · 2026-09 ~ 2026-11 · wip · hitl-chatbot
My part: one of four engineers; I joined a running proof of concept in 2026-09. Teammates built the webhook core, most dashboard pages and the intent router.

  • Evaluated the new retrieval against the existing knowledge base on the client's test questions before switching (recall@1 56.8% vs 91.3%) and kept it behind a default-off switch with one-variable rollback. (B2)
  • Built a second RAG knowledge source for a human-in-the-loop support chatbot: operator text/PDF upload, a background indexer chunking and embedding into Qdrant, live SSE progress, and generation-safe re-indexing. (B1)
  • Built chatbot evaluation tooling: a runner executing the client's 633-case multi-turn test set with concurrency and resume, and a React/TypeScript app comparing runs and grading answers. (B4)
  • Prototyped an agent answer engine (tool loop over the existing rate, branch and knowledge resolvers) beside the fixed chain, keeping must-not-fail rules in code: step cap, admin handoff on failure, reply guardrails. (B3)

Parallel LLM serving evaluation · 2026-10 · wip, one-day spike · llm-serving
My part: sole author of a one-day spike.

  • Built a concurrent streaming load tester for OpenAI-compatible LLM servers (Python asyncio + httpx) reporting per-request TTFT and throughput; it showed Ollama serving 4 concurrent requests one at a time (TTFT 0.1 → 4.4 s). (B1)
  • Root-caused Ollama's failure to parallelise Qwen 3.5: its scheduler pins hybrid-architecture models to a single slot, traced to an unfixed upstream llama.cpp recurrent-state issue, plus a desktop-app setting forcing one parallel slot. (B2)
  • Designed a continuous-batching test (long request at 0 s, short at 5 s) that separates continuous from static batching; on vLLM the late request got its first token 0.4 s after send. (B3)
  • Evaluated vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and Ollama against six serving requirements for a 5–10 concurrent-request target, recommending vLLM for the GPU server and advising against MTP speculative decoding at that load. (B4)

RAG strategy comparison: Simple RAG, GraphRAG, LightRAG · 2026-10 · wip · graphrag
My part: sole developer, working with an AI coding agent.

  • Built a research prototype that compares Simple RAG, GraphRAG and LightRAG side by side over one Neo4j-backed corpus, holding chunks, embeddings, LLMs, prompt and an 8k-token context budget constant. (B1)
  • Implemented GraphRAG from its paper without the official library: LLM entity extraction with gleaning, hierarchical Leiden communities, community reports, and local and map-reduce global query modes. (B2)
  • Implemented LightRAG's dual-level retrieval: question keyword extraction, entity- and relationship-level vector search in Neo4j, and local, global and hybrid query modes fitted to a shared token budget. (B3)
  • Built an indexing pipeline with a disk cache of LLM calls keyed by model and prompt, 1–8 worker threads, live progress, and per-call token and cost tracking in SQLite. (B4)
  • Built a FastAPI and Next.js comparison UI that streams three answers in parallel over Server-Sent Events, with each strategy's retrieved context, a knowledge-graph browser and a scored question history. (B5)
  • Analysed indexing at 100k-chunk scale, estimating about $255 of GraphRAG extraction cost, and proposed range indexes, windowed embedding writes and a streaming merge. (B6: estimated and proposed, not built)

Chatbot core template · 2026-11 · wip · chatbot-core
My part: sole author of the research and the prototype. The engineering brief was written by others.

  • Prototyped a reusable Python chatbot core that each client installs as a version-pinned wheel, proving two mock clients (insurance, real estate) could add business tools without changing the core. (B1)
  • Compared agent frameworks (Tau, Pydantic AI, LangGraph, a TypeScript option) and wrapped the chosen Tau agent loop behind one bridge module, enforced by import-linter contracts. (B2)
  • Designed an extension standard (tools, skills, instructions, guardrails) and fail-closed message guardrails, used by a mock insurance client to block political and violent topics with a decision model. (B3)
  • Built conversation persistence, streaming events, per-reply token usage and cost, an MCP server adapter, and a CLI and Streamlit app for developers to chat with each client's agent. (B4)
  • Wrote the versioned developer docs site in Astro Starlight and drafted the design-doc response to the engineering brief, including the trade-offs the prototype exposed. (B5)

Decision-model R&D · decision-model
My part: sole developer of the repo. The decision and chat models are third-party hosted models.

  • Prototyped a task-delegation tool: a decision model picks owner, type and severity, code checks capacity caps against live Jira load, and a chat model streams the reasoning. (B5)
  • Prototyped a support-chatbot intent router on a decision model (15 intents plus handoff and notify probabilities), matching the expected action on 42 of 43 labelled messages. (B6: the router was tuned on the same messages, so this is not held-out accuracy)

Data pipelines and analytics (2023 → 2026)

This theme runs through the whole period: customer segmentation for loyalty and point-of-sale clients, Airflow pipelines for exhibition, retail and energy data, and time-series storage for detection and sensor results.

Sensor telemetry aggregation pipeline · 2025-08 ~ 2026-07 · shipped · sensor-pipeline
My part: sole developer of the pipeline. The InfluxDB ingestion and the dashboard sit outside it.

  • Built an Apache Airflow pipeline that aggregates raw InfluxDB energy telemetry (solar, grid, time-of-use, voltage, current, power) into 15-minute, hourly and daily TimescaleDB tables, in production since 2025-09. (B1)
  • Traced intermittent production task failures and lost top-of-hour points (13 of 24 on one day) to 9 DAGs firing in the same minute on a 2-vCPU host, then staggered the schedules. (B3)
  • Found a 1.84 GB Airflow XCom table caused by tasks returning whole DataFrames, and changed the final task to return a row count; merged batched ON CONFLICT upserts after verifying 0 duplicates. (B4)
  • Investigated a solar feed silent for about six months, using per-day row counts to show all 4 inverters stopped within minutes, pointing to a site gateway fault rather than the pipeline. (B5)
  • Designed a thin-DAG pattern: each metric shares one Flux query, transform and upsert module across its resolutions, with local-time (UTC+7) windows and a 5-minute ingestion-delay offset. (B2)
  • Added Discord failure alerts, a weekly heartbeat DAG and 30-day log cleanup, and fixed a heartbeat task that sent duplicate messages and false failure alerts. (B6)

Legacy point-of-sale sync and membership analytics · 2024-08 ~ 2025-02 · shipped · legacy-pos
My part: data sync, analytics pipelines and dashboard APIs. A teammate built the member app and the first Debezium setup.

  • Built Airflow ELT that copies 7 sales and payment tables daily from a legacy MySQL 5.5 point-of-sale database into PostgreSQL, after Debezium change data capture proved unworkable on the old MySQL version. (B1)
  • Built an Airflow Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) segmentation pipeline that identifies customers by payment card, scores them into quantile segments every 12 hours and stores the cut-offs for the dashboard. (B2)
  • Moved a slow top-products dashboard query into a 12-hourly Airflow pre-aggregation table with indexes, serving daily or monthly rankings by product group and by delivery or dine-in sales. (B3)
  • Built Django REST dashboard APIs for revenue by payment type and bank, average customers per bill and spend per customer, with gap-filled daily and monthly time series. (B4)

Exhibition booth visitor analytics · event-booth
My part: main developer of the ETL pipeline and the dashboard API. Teammates built most of the dashboard frontend.

  • Built an Apache Airflow ETL pipeline that turned IP camera face-capture events from 12 booth camera zones into hourly visitor-count and age/gender aggregates for an exhibition analytics dashboard. (B1; Numbers: 13 cameras at the booth, the 12 zones plus 1 wide-angle, user-reported)
  • Precomputed dashboard data as Airflow cache collections, so API requests read daily and per-cluster summaries instead of recomputing clusters. (B5)

LINE loyalty platform: RFM segmentation · 2023-02 ~ 2023-05 · shipped · line-crm

Voice and video media-merge service · 2025-07 ~ 2025-09 · shipped · media-merge
My part: main developer of the worker; the API was built with three teammates. A teammate set up the NVIDIA runtime and the first GPU re-render.

  • Built a RabbitMQ-driven ffmpeg worker that turns a chatbot session into a personalised video: text-to-speech greeting, preset clips with transitions, and a 9:16 version with Thai text overlays. (B1)
  • Replaced MoviePy with ffmpeg and added encoder auto-selection (NVIDIA NVENC, Apple VideoToolbox, others) with per-call CPU fallback, so one worker runs on a Mac or an NVIDIA server. (B2)
  • Fixed duplicate processing across parallel GPU workers with an atomic Postgres task claim, database-tracked retries with requeue, and per-worker temp directories. (B3)
  • Designed preset-video selection from three chatbot answers, then made it prefer the preset the chatbot sends and report the preset used, fixing mismatched video covers. (B4)
  • Wrote the worker's error-handling layer as an Either-monad pipeline with retry decorators and Discord failure alerts, so failed sessions surface with their error message. (B5)

Queues, workers and event streams behind the AI systems

  • Replaced in-process daemon-thread dispatch with a Celery + Redis job queue (chunked chord tasks, idempotent retries, row locks, stale-job reaper), so inference jobs survive restarts and out-of-memory kills. (retail-shelf B2)
  • Moved server-sent progress events to a Redis pub/sub broker with per-user channels, fixing lost events across 5 web workers and closing a cross-tenant event leak. (retail-shelf B3)
  • Migrated the pipeline from Kafka frame streaming to a RabbitMQ task queue when requirements moved to upload-then-process, adding manual ack, heartbeats for multi-minute jobs and task progress tracking. (road-safety B2)
  • Wrote a reusable long-running RabbitMQ task worker with a heartbeat thread, manual ack/nack and PostgreSQL task-status and progress tracking, so multi-minute video jobs ran on parallel workers. (classroom B2)
  • Moved the Django backend from WSGI to ASGI (gunicorn + uvicorn workers), chosen over a threaded WSGI server because long-lived SSE connections would exhaust its thread pool. (hitl-chatbot B5)

  • Added date-range CSV exports of members, receipts and shipping addresses for the admin team, and a public shop-ranking API that ranks onsite shops by approved revenue. (line-crm B4)

Decisions and production support

Pointers to bullets above where the result was a decision, a fix in production or a security gain.

  • Decisions backed by measurement: kept a weaker retrieval source switched off (hitl-chatbot B2); traced a detection plateau to the data, not the model (retail-shelf B5); chose batch sync after change data capture proved unworkable (legacy-pos B1); audited a client database before building on it (hitl-chatbot B6); advised against speculative decoding at the target load (llm-serving B4).
  • Production support: diagnosed task failures, table growth and a silent sensor feed in a live pipeline (sensor-pipeline B3–B5); fixed a production LDAP login failure (life-insurance-cms B5).
  • Security: closed a cross-tenant event leak (retail-shelf B3); sanitised rich-text HTML against script injection (life-insurance-cms B4).

Collaboration & mentorship

Nothing about mentoring, onboarding or helping teammates is recorded in evidence yet: verify asks about it for each project. What evidence shows is code written for others to build on:

Interview stories

Measuring a new retrieval source before switching to it

  • Situation: In 2026-09 I joined a running proof of concept: a human-in-the-loop support chatbot for a currency-exchange chain with about 25 branches, answering customers on LINE and Messenger.
  • Task: Add a second knowledge source that operators manage themselves, without risking the answers customers already got.
  • Action: I built the source end to end: upload, a background indexer into Qdrant, live progress over SSE and generation-safe re-indexing. Its retrieval sat behind a switch that returns the same context shape as the old path. Before switching, I wrote an evaluation command and a relabelled test set, and ran old against new on the same question pool.
  • Result: The new source was much weaker: recall@1 56.8% against 91.3%, and 90.8% → 56.3% on the 174 cases both could score. I traced it to short articles that attract unrelated questions and to overlapping score distributions. The switch shipped default-off, with rollback by one environment variable.

Source: hitl-chatbot Context, What I Did 1–3, Numbers row 1–2, B1–B2

Finding why a production pipeline lost data

  • Situation: An Airflow pipeline I built alone aggregates energy telemetry from InfluxDB into TimescaleDB, in production since 2025-09. In 2026-07 the production host kept raising alerts.
  • Task: Find the cause of the task failures and the missing data points.
  • Action: From logs, container state and the database, I showed that 9 DAGs fired in the same minute on a 2-vCPU host with no swap. That pushed DAG imports past their timeout and dropped top-of-hour points. I staggered the schedules. I also found a 1.84 GB XCom table caused by tasks returning whole DataFrames, and checked for 0 duplicate keys before adding a unique index.
  • Result: The root cause and an eight-change remediation plan are written up, and the fixes merged. Whether the data loss stopped after deploy is not yet confirmed.

Source: sensor-pipeline Context, What I Did 8–11, Numbers rows 4, 5, 6, 9, B3–B4

Building a shelf-analytics platform alone

  • Situation: A retail-research client collects smartphone photos of store shelves and wanted to sell shelf analytics reports to consumer brands. A proof of concept existed.
  • Task: Rebuild it as a multi-tenant product: detect products, logos and empty slots, name the brands, and show analytics per survey.
  • Action: As sole committer, I designed and built it end to end: one-pass YOLO detection and DINOv2 brand matching on Modal GPUs, a Django REST API and Next.js dashboards. I replaced daemon-thread dispatch with a Celery and Redis queue so jobs survive restarts, and moved progress events to Redis pub/sub, which closed a cross-tenant event leak. When accuracy stalled, I trained two architectures to test whether the model was the limit.
  • Result: The platform runs on a production host, and the client was trialling it in 2026-09. Both architectures reached the same per-class profile, logo AP50 0.54 against product 0.92 on 23 validation images, which pointed to the data, not the model.

Source: retail-shelf Context, B1–B3, B5, Numbers rows 1–2

Testing a hosted vision model on real shelf images

  • Situation: An internal R&D project tried hosted "decision models" on problems from the company's earlier projects, including brand recognition for the retail-shelf product.
  • Task: Measure whether a vision decision model could name brands on real shelf crops, and at what cost.
  • Action: I built the model client and an image send policy after the vendor rejected large images, stored predictions by fingerprint so re-runs skipped unchanged images, and built evaluation pages with per-brand metrics. I then compared a second model on the same images.
  • Result: 89% top-1 accuracy on 739 labelled crops in 6 categories (74%–96% per category). The second model matched all 44 comparison images at about one-ninth of the cost. The retail-shelf project then took the model in as a second brand recognizer, on a branch not yet merged.

Source: decision-model Context, B1–B3, Numbers rows 1–4; retail-shelf B6

Finding why an LLM server answered one request at a time

  • Situation: A team needed a self-hosted Qwen 3.5 server for 5–10 concurrent requests. On Ollama, concurrent requests ran one after another.
  • Task: Find out why, and choose a serving engine, in a one-day spike.
  • Action: I built a streaming load tester that reports time to first token per request. It showed a staircase: 0.1, 1.5, 2.9 and 4.4 s for four requests. I traced the cause to Ollama's scheduler, which pins hybrid-architecture models to one slot because of an unfixed upstream llama.cpp issue. I also designed a test that tells continuous batching from static batching.
  • Result: On vLLM the late request got its first token 0.4 s after sending. I recommended vLLM for the GPU server and advised against speculative decoding at that load. The GPU-server run is still pending.

Source: llm-serving Context, What I Did 1–4, Numbers rows 3–4, B1–B4
